nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a graph and let $(E_j)_{j \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a family of relations, each a predicate on finite lists of vertices of $G$. Relation symbol $0$ is interpreted as the edge relation of $G$: it holds of a list exactly when the list is $[a, b]$ for vertices $a, b$ with an edge from $a$ to $b$. For $i \ge 1$, relation symbol $i$ is interpreted as $E_{i-1}$.
nodes.title: Interpretation of relation symbols in a graph

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a graph with vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ and edge table $t$, a finite list of booleans. For vertices $a, b < n$, there is an edge from $a$ to $b$ exactly when the entry of $t$ at position $an + b$ (counting from $0$) is true; a position beyond the end of $t$ counts as false.
nodes.title: Edge relation of a graph

nodes.summary: For a class $K$ of graphs, this is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of pairs of a natural number and a list of booleans, to a graph $G \in K$ with $n$ vertices whose edge table has length exactly $n^2$.
nodes.title: Encodings of a graph class as a decision problem

nodes.summary: A class $K$ of graphs is existential second-order definable if there are a natural number $k$, a first-order formula $\varphi$ and a boolean $e$ such that every graph $G$ with $n$ vertices whose edge table has length exactly $n^2$ satisfies the following: if $n > 0$, then $G \in K$ if and only if $G$ satisfies the existential second-order sentence $(k, \varphi)$; if $n = 0$, then $G \in K$ if and only if $e$ is true.
nodes.title: Existential second-order definable graph classes

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a graph with $n > 0$ vertices, $k$ a natural number and $\varphi$ a first-order formula. Then $G$ satisfies the existential second-order sentence $(k, \varphi)$ if there are relations $R_0, \dots, R_{k-1}$, each a predicate on finite lists of vertices of $G$, such that $\varphi$ holds in $G$ when relation symbol $0$ is interpreted as the edge relation (holding exactly of the lists $[a, b]$ with an edge…
nodes.title: Satisfaction of an existential second-order sentence

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a graph, let $\rho$ assign a vertex $\rho(j)$ of $G$ to each variable $x_j$ ($j \in \mathbb{N}$), and let $S$ assign to each relation symbol $i \in \mathbb{N}$ a predicate $S_i$ on finite lists of vertices of $G$. Truth of a formula is defined by recursion: $x_a = x_b$ holds when $\rho(a) = \rho(b)$; relation symbol $i$ applied to the variables $x_{a_1}, \dots, x_{a_m}$ holds when $S_i$ holds of the list…
nodes.title: Evaluation of a first-order formula in a graph

nodes.summary: Variables and relation symbols are indexed by natural numbers. Formulas are built from equations $x_a = x_b$ between variables and atomic formulas applying a relation symbol $i$ to a finite list of variables, by negation, conjunction, disjunction and existential quantification $\exists \varphi$, which binds variable $0$ of $\varphi$ (de Bruijn indexing).
nodes.title: First-order formulas over graphs

nodes.summary: A finite graph is a pair $(n, t)$ of a natural number $n$, the number of vertices, and a finite list $t$ of booleans, read as a row-major edge table. The length of $t$ is not required to be $n^2$.
nodes.title: Finite graphs as edge tables

nodes.summary: A class $K$ of graphs is isomorphism-closed if for every $G_1 \in K$, every graph $G_2$ isomorphic to $G_1$ also belongs to $K$.
nodes.title: Isomorphism-closed graph classes

nodes.summary: Graphs $G_1$ and $G_2$ are isomorphic if they have the same number of vertices and there is a bijection $\sigma$ from the vertices of $G_1$ to the vertices of $G_2$ such that for all vertices $a, b$ of $G_1$, there is an edge from $a$ to $b$ in $G_1$ if and only if there is an edge from $\sigma(a)$ to $\sigma(b)$ in $G_2$.
nodes.title: Isomorphic graphs

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a class of finite graphs, each given as a pair $(n, t)$ of a number $n$ of vertices and a row-major edge table $t$ (a list of booleans), and suppose that $K$ is closed under graph isomorphism. Then the decision problem that accepts exactly the bitstrings decoding to a member $(n, t)$ of $K$ whose edge table has length $n^2$ is in NP if and only if $K$ is definable in existential second-order logic: there…
nodes.title: Fagin's theorem: NP is existential second-order logic

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
